6686:if-true: `if (true) await earlier;` instead of `if (earlier !== null) await earlier;`: `earlier` is either null or a promise, and awaiting null resolves in the same microtask turn, so no request is ordered differently (the requests of one connection already queue behind a promise).
7383:if-false: `if (false)` for the guard `response.destroyed || response.writableEnded` of send(): Node 22 ignores a write to a destroyed response and a second end(), so the guard only skips work; no answer, state or socket differs (defense in depth, never the only protection: every path that calls send() returns after it).
7402:swap ||: `response.destroyed && response.writableEnded` instead of `||`: the same guard weakened; with writableEnded true or the response destroyed, Node ignores the second write exactly as above, so no observable difference.
7570:swap >=: `status > 300` instead of `status >= 300`: the server never answers with status 300 (the statuses of result.cjs are 200, 201, 202 and 4xx and 5xx), so the boundary value is not reachable; tests\boundaries.test.cjs enumerates the statuses the service emits.
